content.text:
Confirmed: the generic-table `of(Transaction, Namespace, String tableName, ...)` signature has stayed `(t, namespace, tableName, …)` ordering ever since `Namespace` support was added in `8852f3a`, but the call site in `TableFactoryRenderer.getTable()` for generic tables passed the arguments in the wrong order (`t, name, namespace, …`) — introduced in the very same commit. That mismatch is exactly what `22f19d7` corrects by swapping back to `t, namespace, name, …`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 8852f3a982336150f16cace5771ae6611134c819

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation.** The fix commit `22f19d7` touches `RowOrDynamicColumnRenderer.java`, `TableFactoryRenderer.java`, `TableRenderer.java`, and many generated files (which are just regenerated snapshots, not hand-written logic). To find the real logic bug rather than cosmetic regen noise, I focused on the one hunk in `TableFactoryRenderer.java` that is a pure logic change:

```
- line("return ", Table, ".of(t, name, namespace, Triggers.getAllTriggers(...));");
+ line("return ", Table, ".of(t, namespace, name, Triggers.getAllTriggers(...));");
```

I then checked the matching static-factory signature generated by `TableRenderer.java` for "generic" tables (tables whose name is supplied at runtime): `of(Transaction t, Namespace namespace, String tableName, ...)`. Using `git log`/`git show` on both files, I traced history back to commit `8852f3a982336150f16cace5771ae6611134c819` ("John Carrino", Aug 23 2015), which is the commit that introduced `Namespace` support end-to-end: it added the `Namespace namespace` parameter to the generated `TableRenderer` factory methods (`of(Transaction t, Namespace namespace, ...)`) and, in the same commit, added the corresponding call site in `TableFactoryRenderer.getTable()`. For the generic-table branch it wrote `Table.of(t, name, namespace, ...)` — swapping `name` and `namespace` relative to the signature it had just defined. `git blame` on the pre-fix line shows it was only touched afterward by a purely cosmetic rename commit (`6a4dfe0`, `_(...)` → `line(...)`), with no logic change, confirming the ordering mistake traces directly to `8852f3a`.

**(2) The specific change.** In `8852f3a`, `TableRenderer.java`'s generated static factory for generic tables takes `(Transaction t, Namespace namespace, String tableName, ...)`, but `TableFactoryRenderer.java`'s generated `getXTable(...)` method body called it as `XTable.of(t, name, namespace, ...)` — i.e., with the `String name` and `Namespace namespace` arguments in the wrong positions. Since `name` is a `String` and `namespace` is a `Namespace`, generated code using a schema with a "generic table name" would fail to type-check at the call site (or at minimum call the wrong overload/arguments), a bug later corrected in `22f19d7`.

**(3) Supporting evidence.** 
- `git show 8852f3a -- TableFactoryRenderer.java` shows the argument-order mistake being introduced alongside the new `Namespace`-aware signature.
- `git show 8852f3a -- TableRenderer.java` shows the corresponding `of(Transaction t, Namespace namespace, ...)` signature being added at the same time, confirming the mismatch.
- `git blame` of the buggy line right before the fix shows no intervening logic change besides a cosmetic rename, so the defect persisted unchanged from `8852f3a` through to `22f19d7`.
- No schema in the repository currently sets a "generic table name" (`genericTableName(...)` is defined in `TableDefinition.java` but never invoked by any schema in this repo), which explains why this latent bug never surfaced as a compile failure or in any previously-generated `.java` file — it was a dormant defect in the code generator's template, only now fixed.

**Uncertainty:** The fix commit `22f19d7` also adds unrelated-looking functionality (`getRawTableName()`, `hasFirstComponentHash`/murmur3 hashing support for row components in `RowOrDynamicColumnRenderer.java`). These look like new feature work (the `hasFirstComponentHash` flag was added earlier in `f016c1d` but was never wired into the row renderer until this commit), rather than fixes for a pre-existing regression — I found no prior commit where that wiring was present and then broken, so I don't classify `f016c1d` as a "bug-introducing" commit with the same confidence; it is better described as an incomplete feature addition rather than a regression. The one clear, verifiable, SZZ-style bug fix in this commit is the argument-order correction in `TableFactoryRenderer.java`, which I'm confident traces to `8852f3a`.
